meta.title: Cessna 172P airframe fasteners placed on the FlightGear c172p model

sources.manual: Cessna Model 172 Series 1977-1986 Service Manual D2065-3-13 Rev 3 (facts and page references; no images reproduced)
sources.extraction: data/c172p-airframe-hardware.json (158 figure sheets, 1,685 callouts, 70 access panels)
sources.model: assets/c172p.glb + assets/cockpit.glb (FlightGear c172p, GPL-2.0, local only)

meta.frame: raw AC3D model frame: meters, +x aft, +y up, +z toward the LEFT wing (same as assets/c172p.glb)
meta.axis_convention: hardware.js: the fastener head sits at `position`, the shank runs along -axis (axis points out of the head / surface)

reference_airplane.configuration: standard wing with metal tanks; McCauley two-piece wheels; wheel speed fairings (on the model); standard front seats; split-back rear seat; 1982-and-on doors and latch

basis_definitions.station from figure: located from a station the manual prints (FS/WS) through the fitted transform
basis_definitions.model geometry: located on the model's own part (strut ends, gear legs, wheels, hinge axes, doors, cockpit objects), snapped where it fastens to skin
basis_definitions.estimated pattern: location or count inferred (drawing proportions, typical pitch/bolt circle); the count is the manual's when it prints one

notes: Every unit is a separate placement (a washer stack of 3 is 3 placements). Quantities are the manual's printed or counted values, x2 for parts drawn for one side.
Items with no printed size get an estimated diameter/length (d_in, len_in) for display; part_number is only what the manual prints.
Access-panel screw counts are not printed (except the Fig 18-11 cover, 6 screws): round plates use 6, perimeter covers and fairings use an estimated pitch.

Wing, aileron and flap hardware sits on the true-scale wing of data/c172p-structure-wing-3d.json (z = WS x 0.0254, NACA 2412 depth), heads on its outer skin; the wing attach and strut-to-wing bolts keep their FlightGear axes, where the structure's fitting holes sit; points taken from FlightGear objects (fuel caps, pitot, vent, lights) are moved with the structure's meta.refit rule. The model's firewall is ~4 in aft of the fitted FS 0, so firewall hardware follows the model's firewall.
Interior hardware (pulleys, bellcranks, turnbuckles, cable runs) sits inside the skin at estimated stations along the cable routes; the model has no internal structure there.
Torques are the manual's for that callout; others: Table 1-1 (text_hardware) applies.
Engine-mounted hardware (cylinder, case, accessory studs) is in data/o320d2j-placements.json and is not repeated here.

Option choices: Cleveland wheels, McCauley hub/capscrew wheels, the integral-bay (wet) wing, infinitely adjustable and auxiliary seats, standby vacuum, circulating fan and encoding altimeter are skipped (counted in skipped_*).

Verified with renders of the placements on the model (wing attach, strut ends, main and nose gear, access plates, fin-root row, tail hinges, engine mount) and with the fit counts above; misplacements found that way were corrected in the anchors.

Engine cowling (Fig 11-1, paras 11-2/11-3): every cowl fastener sits on the model's own seams: the aft edges of fuselage_cowling_top / fuselage_cowling (firewall shock mounts), the side parting lines, the nose-cap ring and the oil-door hole; heads 0.8 mm proud of the outer skin, axes along the skin normal. The manual gives the fastener types but no counts except the air-box 4 + 4; shock mounts are counted from the drawing, the rest are estimated pitches (qty_basis says which).

Skin rivets: the manual prints no production rivet pattern for skins or cowling. It gives the Fig 18-13 leading-edge rib rivet table (placed), repair patterns only (Fig 18-4 pitch 4-8D / 6D, edge distance 2D; Fig 18-10 1 in max; Fig 18-11 access-hole doubler 10 rivets), para 18-62 (firewall periphery angles: steel MS20450; shock-mount brackets: aluminum MS20470; no count) and para 18-71 (bonded cowl seams may be replaced by one 3/32 2117-AD rivet per running inch). Only the cowl nose-cap joint, the shock-mount brackets and hinge leaves get rivets here; general skin rivets are not invented.

Audit additions (figure by figure): cowling seams and oil door; tail tie-down ring; main-gear step bracket bolts; wheel-fairing mounting-plate, scraper and access-door screws; nose-fairing cover/scraper/door screws; cabin-door hinge-leaf screws and rivets and doorstop screws; baggage-door pad and hinge-strap screws; fuel filler adapter, transmitter and tank-strap screws; spinner screws; elevator and rudder tip screws; trim-tab hinge pin and rivets; dorsal screws; lights re-counted from Section 16 (Figs 16-6 sheet 3, 16-7, 16-8).

assemblies.title: Wing attach (standard wing)
assemblies.applicability: Standard wing, all 172 1977-86 incl. 172P. Item 15 (wing-mounted landing light) beginning with 17275035 and F1722135 & on (i.e. 1982 172P onward). Left wing drawn (stall warning unit and landing light are left-wing items); right wing mirror without 15/17/18.

assemblies.title: Horizontal stabilizer attach and elevator hinges
Main landing gear
assemblies.applicability: all; elbow (*) thru 1981 Models; elbow 21/nut 22/O-ring 23 beginning with 1982 Models; fuselage fairings (17) split thru 17271034/F17201749, one-piece from 17271035/F17201750 (so one-piece on 172P; service replacements are split); items 20 (star) used only with wheel fairings

assemblies.title: Main wheel speed fairings
assemblies.applicability: Effectivity columns: (dot) 17263459 thru 17271569 / F17201235 thru F17201794; (*) 17271570 thru 17273369, F17201795 thru F17202029, 17276575 & On; (*) 17273370 thru 17276574, F17202030 and On. 172P (17274010-17276654) falls in the * columns: access door (*7) or plug (*9) inset variants; dot items (door 8 latch) apply to earlier serials. Exact mapping of each * inset to its column is indicated by pointing-hand symbols (ambiguous in scan).

assemblies.title: Main wheels and brakes (McCauley two-piece)
assemblies.applicability: McCauley two-piece wheel option; elbow (15) thru 1981 Models; elbow 28/nut 29/O-ring 30 beginning with 1982 Models

assemblies.title: Nose wheel speed fairing
assemblies.applicability: Same effectivity columns as Fig 5-2: dot 17263459-17271569; * 17271570-17273369 & 17276575 & on; * 17273370-17276574. 172P uses * variants (plug 11 / door 9 insets).

assemblies.title: Brake master cylinders (1979 and on)
assemblies.applicability: BEGINNING WITH 1979 MODELS (applies to 172P); two cylinders, immediately forward of pilot's rudder pedals

assemblies.title: Aileron control system: cabin and wing-root pulleys
assemblies.applicability: Legend on sheet 2. * = THRU 17269874 & F17201829; dot = 17269875 & ON, F17201830 THRU F17202233 (dot items apply to 172P).

assemblies.title: Aileron control system: cabin-top pulley clusters
Control U and control wheels

assemblies.title: Propeller and spinner bulkheads
